title: Inquest scheduled into death of Babak Saidi
article: A coroner's inquest into the death of Babak Saidi in December 2017 that was paused by the pandemic has been scheduled to begin later this month.

East region Ottawa office regional supervising coroner Dr. Louise McNaughton-Filion released the details of the rescheduled inquest on Monday afternoon. The notice indicates the inquest will hear from approximately 12 witnesses, over what's expected to take eight days starting on Wednesday, April 20.
Dr. Bob Reddoch has been assigned as the inquest officer, with Prahbu Rajan and Uko Abara assigned as inquest counsel.

Reddoch had been assigned to this inquest back in 2020, when the inquest had been scheduled to begin on March 30. The start of the COVID-19 pandemic scuttled all scheduled coroner's inquests across Ontario.

Saidi, 43, died after being shot five times during a struggle with two officers on Dec. 23, 2017, after going to the SDG OPP office in Morrisburg for a routine check-in. An inquest is mandatory given the death was as a result of an officer's use of force.

The Special Investigations Unit completed its examination of what happened that day in 2019, and determined there was no basis to lay any criminal charges against the officers involved. The OPP's intention had been to arrest Saidi on new charges when he came to the office for his mandated check-in, but things went awry and resulted in a scuffle that saw a Taser fired at Saidi with no effect, and the report concluded the officer had no choice but to fire at close range.

Saidi's family has consistently called for an inquest into what happened that day, noting he had a diagnosed mental illness and saying they hope the inquest can make recommendations to ensure similar situations do not deteriorate so quickly, or result in the death of someone who is mentally ill.
The inquest is scheduled to begin at 9:30 a.m., and is taking place at the Holiday Inn & Suites, 101 Kanata Ave., in Kanata.
